newsitem.title: INDIA: India Hind Motors Lancer launch in June 98.
newsitem.headline: India Hind Motors Lancer launch in June 98.

text.p: Indian car maker Hindustan Motors Ltd will launch Mitsubishi Motor Corp's Lancer car in India in June 1998, the company's executive director said on Tuesday.
"The plant near Madras should be ready by March, and the Lancer should hit the roads by June 1998," A. Sankara Narayanan, executive director, Hindustan Motors told Reuters.
He said the Lancer will cost about 600,000 rupees ($16,800) for the base model. "The precise price will be fixed just before we launch it."
Sankara Narayanan said Hindustan Motors would make 30,000 Lancers at full capacity, and would come to the market with two models -- a 1.5 litre petrol and a 2.0 litre diesel.
Hindustan Motors has invested 3.24 billion rupees in a new facility to manufacture Lancers under licence from Japan's Mitsubishi Motor Corp.
Sankara Narayanan said there was no equity collaboration with Mitsubishi at present. "The complete investment in the facility has been made by Hindustan Motors."
The Lancer will be the second car to be made in India under a licensee agreement. It follows the Uno, manufactured by Premier Automobiles Ltd under licence from Italy's Fiat S.p.A.
It will compete head on with Hindustan Motors' equal joint venture with General Motors Corp, General Motors India Ltd, which makes the Opel Astra.
The Association of Indian Automobile Manufacturers estimates that vehicle production will top a million units by 2000, up from 404,040 units in 1996/97 (April-March).
This has drawn some of the world's leading car makers to India.
South Korea's Daewoo Corp and Ford Motor Co of the U.S. have already launched their cars in India, and Honda Motor Company, Hyundai Motor Co, and Toyota Motor Corp are in the process of doing so.
Suzuki Motor Corp's joint venture with the Indian government, Maruti Udyog Ltd, dominates the car market with 80 percent share. ($ = 35.7 Indian Rupees)
